_doc: SPEC-V6: the DECLARATIVE half of WebMCP. Open a slot by hand → the details form becomes a browser-published tool (clinic_booking_form). The agent FILLS it; the page shows 'Filled in by your agent'; an agent-attributed submit is refused and counted; the person's trusted press moves it to review and books. Chrome-only (ChatGPT ignores declarative forms).
The form does not exist until a person picks a slot — so neither does its tool.

The browser now publishes the form as a tool (the harness sees it in the platform's own list). The FILL is Chrome's declarative machinery — driven by the browser's agent UI, not by this CDP harness — so it is checked by hand with the Model Context Tool Inspector (evals/manual/README.md). What IS provable here: no autosubmit, and a submit the person did not make is refused and counted.
A submit the person did not make (dispatched by script) is refused and counted; the form stays put.

eval: (() => { const f = document.querySelector('form[data-clinic-step="details"]'); f.dispatchEvent(new Event('submit', { bubbles: true, cancelable: true })); return 'synthetic-submit'; })()

_doc: The person fills it (trusted keystrokes) and presses Review — the form moves for them, not for a script.
Name, date of birth and phone arrive from the patient on file (PatientOnFile; the labelled sample under ?test=1). The form starts from them — nothing is retyped.

The TRUSTED press ran the real path: with the date of birth on file the form reaches Review (headless Chrome cannot type a native date, but it no longer has to). Either way the blocked counter never moved for a real press — it stays at the one synthetic attempt.
